title: One agenda owner for the Schedule tab: write-through mutations + live refresh
acceptance: adoptInvite(invites, inv): an invite whose token is already in the list is replaced in place (order kept, other rows keep identity); an unknown token is appended; a null/undefined invite returns the SAME array reference.

applyMutation(state, {kind:'book', entryId:E, invite: confirmed slotAt X}) -> E is gone from state.entries AND bookedMarkersFrom(state.invites, calendarEntryIdsOf(state)) contains a marker at isoToDateSlot(X). (Today the hour is drawn free: the tab drops the card at useScheduleTab.ts:372 and never adopts the returned invite.)

applyMutation(state, {kind:'accept_proposal', invite: confirmed, entryId:E}) -> the invite leaves bucketInvites(...).attention and lands in .upcoming of the SAME list the grid reads, and effectsFor('accept_proposal') = {refetchEntries:true, notify:true} so the stale pending card for E (approval_kind cleared server-side, db/pipeline.ts:3130-3158) is not left offering a Confirm that would reschedule the accepted time onto a guessed cell.

applyMutation(state, {kind:'cancel', invite: pending (slotAt null)}) -> the grid marker for its old hour disappears and bucketInvites puts it in .awaiting - both derived from one invites array, no second copy.

effectsFor(kind) is total over the recruiter verbs: book, accept_proposal -> refetchEntries true; cancel, no_show, decline_proposals, resolve_reconcile, reinvite, meeting_url -> refetchEntries false; every verb except meeting_url -> notify true (notifyDataChanged, so the Pipeline board and Decisions refresh).

Source contract: useScheduleInviteLifecycle.ts no longer calls sharedGetJson('/api/schedule') - the panel receives invites/truncated/loadedAt as props from the owner, so one tab mount issues exactly one GET /api/schedule by construction rather than by in-flight coalescing.

Source contract: the owner hook subscribes useLiveRefresh(reload) - a data-changed signal from another tab or window (e.g. a candidate drawer move) reloads /api/pipeline + /api/schedule once (coalesced), where today both are mount-only snapshots (useScheduleTab.ts:161-163).
premise: app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleTab.ts:70 - the tab keeps its own `invites` state; app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleInviteLifecycle.ts:35 - the lifecycle panel keeps a second, independent `invites` state for the same GET /api/schedule list.

app/features/hiring/schedule/ScheduleTab.tsx:182-184 renders <InviteLifecyclePanel /> as a CHILD of ScheduleTab, while app/features/shared/sharedGet.ts:9-11 justifies in-flight coalescing because the two are 'siblings' and says passing data down is the better fix 'where one component owns the other' - which is this case.

app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleTab.ts:330-349,371-373 - a successful grid book drops the card from `entries` and never adopts the returned invite (route answers {invite} at app/api/schedule/route.ts:291); bookedMarkersFrom (scheduleTabDerived.ts) only draws confirmed invites from the stale list, so the just-booked hour renders as free until a full reload, and the panel never hears of the booking at all.

app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleInviteLifecycle.ts:73 - panel actions (accept_proposal from ScheduleInviteAttentionSection.tsx:54, cancel, no_show) patch only the panel's copy; the tab's `entries` and `invites` stay as loaded at mount (useScheduleTab.ts:161-163).

app/api/schedule/route.ts:197-261 - `book` checks only entry.status === 'active'; for an entry whose invite is already confirmed it calls rescheduleScheduleInvite with {recruiter:true} (no cap). So a stale pending card left behind after accept_proposal (approve_event clears approval_kind, app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:3130-3158) can move the candidate's accepted time to the card's seeded cell with one Confirm click.

grep -rn 'notifyDataChanged\|useLiveRefresh' app/features/hiring/schedule app/schedule -> no matches: Schedule mutations (which advance pipeline entries server-side, route.ts:274 and :433) announce nothing to the board, and the tab subscribes to nothing.
rollback: Client-only change with no route, schema or catalog edits: the commit series reverts cleanly because the two hooks' public return shapes are preserved for their render components and the new module is additive; reverting restores the two independent fetches and sharedGet coalescing, which is untouched.
runner_up: Collapse useScheduleTab's 20 independent useState latches (entries/error/actionError/busy/creatingIv/prepEntry/transcriptEntry/lastDir...) into one reducer with an explicit load/act status FSM - worth doing, but it changes no behaviour a recruiter sees, whereas the shared agenda closes a real stale-Confirm rebooking path.
body:
## Summary
The Schedule tab holds the same invite agenda twice - once in useScheduleTab for the grid, once in useScheduleInviteLifecycle for the lifecycle panel it renders as a child - and neither copy learns about the other's mutations or about anything that happened outside the tab. Make ScheduleTab the one owner of the agenda (entries + invites), route every recruiter mutation through a pure write-through module, and subscribe the owner to the app's live-refresh bus.

## Description
Today a grid Confirm books the invite server-side but the tab drops the card without adopting the returned invite, so the booked hour is drawn free and the panel's Upcoming list never shows the booking. In the other direction, accepting a candidate's proposed time in the panel advances the pipeline entry server-side (approval cleared) while the tab keeps the candidate as a pending card with a guessed cell; the `book` route treats a Confirm on an already-confirmed invite as a recruiter reschedule with no cap, so one click moves the accepted time onto a guess. sharedGet.ts papers over the duplicate GET with in-flight coalescing and itself says the better fix is passing data down where one component owns the other - ScheduleTab does own the panel. And no Schedule mutation calls notifyDataChanged, although book and accept_proposal advance board entries.

The move: a pure `scheduleAgenda.ts` (adoptInvite, applyMutation, effectsFor) plus an owner hook state in useScheduleTab that the panel consumes via props. Write-through from the client's own mutations is rung 1 of the invalidation hierarchy (client-state / invalidation-strategy); useLiveRefresh is rung 2 for changes made elsewhere; the existing focus-driven interview poll stays a refetch trigger, not the freshness design.

## Flow
1. Write scheduleAgenda.test.ts cases 1-5 against the pure module; they fail (module absent).
2. Implement scheduleAgenda.ts: adoptInvite, applyMutation(state, {kind, entryId?, invite}), effectsFor(kind), reusing bookedMarkersFrom and bucketInvites unchanged.
3. useScheduleTab owns {entries, invites, truncated, loadedAt}; `act` adopts the book response via applyMutation; expose `runAgendaAction` for the panel.
4. useScheduleInviteLifecycle takes the agenda + runner as arguments instead of fetching; InviteLifecyclePanel receives them from ScheduleTab (Defer + dynamic stay).
5. After each mutation, honour effectsFor: refetch /api/pipeline when refetchEntries, notifyDataChanged when notify; subscribe useLiveRefresh(load) in the owner.
6. Update docs/features/scheduling/README.md (the agenda now has one owner and announces its writes).

## Expected impact
The grid and the lifecycle panel can no longer disagree about which hours are taken or which invites need attention; the stale-Confirm path that could reschedule a just-accepted proposal onto a guessed cell closes; the Pipeline board and Decisions update when the Schedule tab books or cancels; one GET /api/schedule per mount by construction.

## Evaluation
Claim: every recruiter mutation on the Schedule tab is reflected in both the grid and the lifecycle panel from one list, and announced to other views.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: contract - node:test over app/features/hiring/schedule/scheduleAgenda.test.ts (cases 1-5) plus two source-contract assertions (cases 6-7), then the integration gate (tsc, lint, test:unit, test:perf).
Result: pending
Gate: none

title: Pending cards act on the invite's real state, not a blind Confirm of a guess
acceptance: liveInviteFor('E', invites) picks deliberately, independent of list order: [confirmed(slotAt X), declined] -> the confirmed one; [declined(newest), pending] -> the pending one; closed-only -> the most recent closed one; none -> null. (Today `new Map(...)` at useScheduleTab.ts:136 keeps whichever row for E comes LAST in the agenda's ORDER BY.)

pendingCardState(entry, null, 'guess', now) -> {kind:'no_link', primary:'send_link', bookSuggested:true}: with no invite and a flat default cell, the primary action is sending the candidate their self-scheduling link, and booking the suggested time is a secondary, explicitly-labelled control.

pendingCardState(entry, pending invite created 50h ago, 'guess', now) -> {kind:'awaiting', sentAt: invite.createdAt, primary:'copy_link'}; the same invite once isScheduleInviteExpired(invite, now) -> {kind:'expired', primary:'reinvite'}.

pendingCardState(entry, invite{proposalStatus:'pending', proposals:[a,b]}, 'guess', now) -> {kind:'proposals', proposals:[a,b]}; each proposal renders an accept control that POSTs {action:'accept_proposal', token, slotAt:a.value} to /api/schedule (the escalation is answered where the candidate's card is, not only in the lifecycle panel).
pendingCardState(entry, invite{needsMoreSlots:true}, 'guess', now) -> {kind:'stuck_no_slots'} with a pointer to the proposals/attention row, never a primary Confirm of the guessed cell.
pendingCardState(entry, confirmed invite, 'booked', now) -> {kind:'booked', primary:'confirm'} - Confirm is the primary action ONLY when the cell is backed by a confirmed invite.

sendLinkNotice({delivery}) maps 'sent' -> scheduleTab.sendLink.sent, 'queued' -> scheduleTab.sendLink.queued, 'failed' -> scheduleTab.sendLink.failed (the truthful claim the /api/schedule/invite route already returns, route.ts:115), and the new keys exist in all four catalogs (i18n:check).

Source contract: ScheduleTabPendingList.tsx keeps a book control carrying data-sim-click="confirm" inside [data-sim-entry] for every non-booked kind, so the guided simulation's fallback click (app/features/shell/simulation/useSimulationWalk.ts:478) still resolves.
premise: app/features/hiring/schedule/ScheduleTypes.ts:30 DEFAULT_SLOT = 'Tue 14:00' and useScheduleTab.ts:153 seeds every entry with neither a confirmed invite nor a parseable legacy detail onto that flat default; scheduleGridSeeds.ts:39 labels it source 'guess'.

app/features/hiring/schedule/ScheduleTabPendingList.tsx:169-177 - the ONLY booking action on every pending card is Confirm (onAct 'approve_event'), rendered identically whether the cell is a confirmed booking or a guess; the guess is marked only by a dashed 'suggested' chip (:99-105).

app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleTab.ts:330-334 - Confirm POSTs {action:'book', dateSlot: picks[e.id]}, i.e. it books whatever cell was seeded, guess included; app/api/schedule/route.ts:179-291 (the book branch) dispatches no candidate message - its only outbound is syncInterviewEvent (route.ts:156-161, :290).

The tab already loads every invite (useScheduleTab.ts:111, :129) but uses them only to seed confirmed cells and draw booked markers (:136-156, :179); pending-link age, candidate proposals and the needs-more-slots stall live only in the separate lifecycle panel (ScheduleInviteAttentionSection.tsx:42-80, ScheduleInviteHistorySection.tsx:15-54), not on the candidate's card.

Nothing on the Schedule tab can send a candidate their self-scheduling link: POST /api/schedule/invite is called from the tab only by the Closed-row re-invite (useScheduleInviteLifecycle.ts:93); first sends live in the pipeline drawer (pipeline/candidate/state/useCandidateLinks.ts:22) and bulk (usePipelineBulk.ts:348).

app/features/hiring/schedule/useScheduleTab.ts:136 - `new Map(invs.filter(i => i.entryId).map(i => [i.entryId, i]))` keeps the LAST invite per entry in the agenda's ORDER BY (schedule-store.ts:370 `(s.slot_at IS NULL) ASC, s.slot_at ASC, s.created_at DESC`), so an entry with a re-invite history resolves to whichever row sorts last rather than its live invite.
rollback: The commit series reverts cleanly: one new pure module + test, a render change in ScheduleTabPendingList, one added action/return field in useScheduleTab, and additive catalog keys appended at the end of the scheduleTab namespace; no route, schema or store change, and the book path the simulation drives is kept intact.
runner_up: Adopt the open L 'Give needs-more-slots a control that actually opens more times' (leftover-develop-2026-09-17, gate direction) - high value, but it needs a product call on what 'more times' means (horizon, hours, or ad-hoc slots) before a builder can start.
body:
## Summary
Every pending card on the Schedule tab offers one booking action - Confirm - and it books whatever cell was seeded, including the flat 'Tue 14:00' guess for a candidate nobody has asked. Derive each card's state from the candidate's live invite and put the next real step first: send the scheduling link, show how long a sent link has waited, accept a proposed time in place, and reserve Confirm as the primary action for cells a confirmed invite backs.

## Description
The product direction recorded in the code is that interview times come from the candidate's own link or their proposals (ScheduleCalendar.tsx:24-28, ScheduleInviteRecruiterControls.tsx:3-8). The pending card contradicts it: with no invite, its only affordance books a default guess, and the book route mails the candidate nothing. The tab already holds every invite and simply does not join them to the cards, so the recruiter decides blind: they cannot see on the card that a link went out three days ago, that the candidate proposed two times, or that the candidate stalled on a fully-booked horizon. Those facts exist only in the lifecycle panel above, keyed by invite rather than by the candidate they are looking at.

The leap: a pure `schedulePendingCardState.ts` resolves (entry, liveInvite, pickSource, now) into one of no_link / awaiting / expired / proposals / stuck_no_slots / booked, and the card renders that state's primary action. 'Send scheduling link' reuses POST /api/schedule/invite and its truthful sent/queued/failed claim; proposal accept reuses the existing accept_proposal verb. The book-a-suggested-time control stays available (labelled as a suggestion, keeping data-sim-click="confirm" for the guided simulation) so no current path is removed. The candidate becomes a participant, not a resource slotted into a default cell (recruiting / candidate-self-scheduling golden path; propose-your-own-times-escalation answered where the recruiter already is).

## Flow
1. Write schedulePendingCardState.test.ts cases 1-7 against the pure module; they fail (module absent).
2. Implement liveInviteFor, pendingCardState and sendLinkNotice (reusing isScheduleInviteExpired and hasPendingProposals).
3. useScheduleTab: return the per-entry live invite and add `sendLink(entry)` (POST /api/schedule/invite, toast from sendLinkNotice, reload with refresh).
4. ScheduleTabPendingList: render the state's primary action; demote Confirm to 'Book suggested time' when kind is not booked, keeping data-sim-click="confirm".
5. Append scheduleTab.sendLink.* and card-state keys to en/cs/de/fr in one commit under the shared-surface lock.
6. Update docs/features/scheduling/README.md (pending-card states and actions).

## Expected impact
A recruiter can no longer book a candidate into a guessed slot without seeing that it is a guess and that sending the link is the intended path; a sent-but-unanswered link, a pending proposal and a stuck candidate are visible and actionable on the card the recruiter is reading; the tab gains the one action its empty-invite state was missing.

## Evaluation
Claim: each pending card's primary action matches the candidate's real invite state, and Confirm is primary only for a confirmed booking.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: contract - node:test over app/features/hiring/schedule/schedulePendingCardState.test.ts (cases 1-7) plus a source-contract assertion on ScheduleTabPendingList.tsx (case 8), then i18n:check and the integration gate.
Result: pending
Gate: none
